_meta.description: NASA GSFC path-table CENTRAL LINE reference points for the modern solar-eclipse accuracy instrument (eclipse-audit 'centerlines' section). Each point: UT instant + the path table's central-line latitude/longitude. THE COLUMN TRAP, now THREE times encountered while building this set: the SEpath tables print northern limit / southern limit / central line as three look-alike coordinate pairs, and casual extraction returns a LIMIT (half a path width of phantom error - the 1999 first fetch returned the northern limit; a 2017 re-fetch did the same; the 2001 Jun 21 11:56 first fetch returned the northern limit 10 49.7S 0 17.9E where the true central line is 11 43.0S 000 26.0E). Every row below is cross-checked: 2017 against the table's own greatest-duration point (18:21:49 at 37 35N 89 07W), 2024 against the greatest-eclipse point (18:17:18 at 25 17.2N 104 08.3W) and the Dallas site geometry, 1999 re-fetched with full column headers, 2023 taken from the explicit three-pair row (third pair = center), the 2001-2020 widening rows verified by sibling-consistency across each event's three instants plus full-column re-fetch of any outlier. The audit compares the scene-umbra ground point at each UT against these and reports both ground km and the SHADOW-PLANE metric (ground x sin sun-altitude, sun altitude from the model - verified within 0.4 deg of the tables' own alt column where captured); ground km are NOT comparable across events (1/sin alt amplification, 6.9x at the low-sun 2026 Spain crossing). The 2001-2020 events were added as the Stage-D2 widening (fetched 2026-08-21): the original 5-event sample's -2.56 arcsec mean was sampling structure, not fleet bias (-0.14 arcsec over 179 syzygies); acceptance decisions read the widened set. The 2021 Dec 04 Antarctica crossing is deliberately NOT tracked here - its anomaly is DIAGNOSED (docs/66: half was the sphere-vs-ellipsoid ground-mapping bug, fixed in besselian umbraGroundAt; the remaining 6.9 arcsec is a verified ordinary apparent-place tail, JPL-closed to 0.05 arcsec) and it now fits the 8 arcsec gate, but promotion to the tracked set is a separate conscious decision.
_meta.source: https://eclipse.gsfc.nasa.gov/SEpath/ (Espenak, NASA GSFC; SEpath1951 + SEpath2001 series), path tables per event as cited in each entry
_meta.timeAxis: UT as printed in the tables (the tables' own deltaT per event applies to their construction, not to this comparison - the scene umbra is evaluated at the same UT instant)
